```plato

    //==
    // The operators.

    // Expand (cantellation, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantellation_(geometry)):
    // faces shrink in place, a quad appears per edge, an n-gon per degree-n
    // vertex. Cube -> rhombicuboctahedron at shrink = sqrt(2) - 1.
    // V' = C, E' = 2E + C, F' = F + V + E.
    Expand(self: PolygonMesh3D, shrink: Number): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMeshOfFaces(
            self.TwistedFacePoints(shrink, Angle(0.0)),
            self.ExpansionFaces((m, c) => [m.ExpandFaceOfEdge(c)]));

    // Snub (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snub_(geometry)): expand with a twist,
    // each edge-quad split into two triangles. Chiral — `twist` > 0 gives one
    // enantiomer, < 0 its mirror. Cube -> snub cube.
    // V' = C, E' = 3E + C, F' = F + V + 2E.
    Snub(self: PolygonMesh3D, shrink: Number, twist: Angle): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMeshOfFaces(
            self.TwistedFacePoints(shrink, twist),
            self.ExpansionFaces((m, c) => m.SnubFacesOfEdge(c)));

    // Bevel (omnitruncation): the Conway identity b = ta — truncate the ambo.
    // Cube -> truncated cuboctahedron. Topologically exact; the vertex faces
    // come out as rectangles rather than squares (the uniform bevel is not
    // reachable by literal truncation), which a caller may accept or relax.
    Bevel(self: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => self.Ambo.Truncate;

    //==
    // # Kis, join and needle on polygon meshes
    //
    // Three more Conway operators
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway_polyhedron_notation), all built from
    // one new vertex block: an APEX per face, the face's centroid pushed out along
    // its own outward normal by `height`. At height zero the apex sits in the face
    // plane, which is the flat fan / rhombic reading of each operator; a positive
    // height raises it, and a negative one dents the face inward.
    //
    //   kis     one triangle per CORNER      (a pyramid raised on every face)
    //   join    one quad per EDGE            (the rhombic form; j = da)
    //   needle  two triangles per EDGE       (n = kd, the dual of truncate)
    //
    // The vertex numbering is the original numbering followed by the face
    // numbering, so again no lookup table is built. Preconditions as for the
    // operators above: a closed manifold mesh with convex faces. Nothing here
    // normalizes the result onto the unit sphere.

    //==
    // The shared vertex block.

    // One apex per face: the face centroid displaced along its outward unit
    // normal. Height is in model units, so scale the mesh first if a comparable
    // spike across several solids is wanted.
    FaceApexPoints(self: PolygonMesh3D, height: Number): Array<Point3D>
        => self.FaceCount.MapRange(f =>
            (self.FaceCentroid(f).PositionVector + self.FaceUnitNormal(f) * height).ToPoint);

    // The apex of a face, read as a vertex of a mesh whose vertex block starts
    // with the original vertices.
    ApexVertex(self: PolygonMesh3D, face: FaceIndex): VertexIndex
        => VertexIndex(self.VertexCount + face.Value);

    //==
    // Kis — raise a pyramid on every face
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kleetope). Every face of arity n becomes n
    // triangles meeting at its apex. Tetrahedron -> triakis tetrahedron,
    // octahedron -> tetrakis hexahedron at the right height. The Conway identity
    // is k = dtd, but the direct construction below needs no dual and so stays
    // exact on a mesh whose face planes pass near the origin.
    // V' = V + F, E' = E + C, F' = C.

    // The triangle a corner contributes: its own edge, closed onto its face's
    // apex. Wound counter-clockwise seen from outside, like the face it replaces.
    KisFaceOfCorner(self: PolygonMesh3D, corner: CornerIndex): Array<VertexIndex>
        => [self.CornerVertex(corner),
            self.CornerDestination(corner),
            self.ApexVertex(self.CornerFace(corner))];

    // One apex per face; one triangle per corner.
    Kis(self: PolygonMesh3D, height: Number): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMeshOfFaces(
            Concatenate(self.Positions, self.FaceApexPoints(height)),
            self.CornerCount.MapRange(c => self.KisFaceOfCorner(CornerIndex(c))));

    //==
    // Join — the Conway identity j = da, one rhombus per edge
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhombic_dodecahedron is jC). Each edge
    // becomes a quadrilateral spanning its two endpoints and the two face apexes
    // beside it, so the result is face-transitive whenever the seed is regular.
    // Height zero (apex = centroid) is the classical join.
    // V' = V + F, E' = 2E, F' = E.

    // The rhombus left where an edge was: endpoint, far face's apex, other
    // endpoint, near face's apex. The far apex comes first because the near
    // face lies to the LEFT of the corner's directed edge, and taking it first
    // would wind the quad clockwise seen from outside.
    // Precondition: `corner` is canonical (one call per undirected edge).
    JoinFaceOfEdge(self: PolygonMesh3D, corner: CornerIndex): Array<VertexIndex>
        => [self.CornerVertex(corner),
            self.ApexVertex(self.CornerFace(self.TwinCorner(corner))),
            self.CornerDestination(corner),
            self.ApexVertex(self.CornerFace(corner))];

    // One apex per face; one quad per undirected edge.
    Join(self: PolygonMesh3D, height: Number): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMeshOfFaces(
            Concatenate(self.Positions, self.FaceApexPoints(height)),
            self.EdgeStitchFaces((m, c) => [m.JoinFaceOfEdge(c)]));

    //==
    // Needle — the Conway identity n = kd, equivalently the dual of truncate
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway_polyhedron_notation). Each edge
    // becomes two long thin triangles reaching between the apexes of the faces
    // on either side of it, which is what the name describes; the original edge
    // survives only as the diagonal neither triangle uses.
    // V' = V + F, E' = 3E, F' = 2E.

    // The two needles of an edge: each endpoint joined to both neighbouring
    // apexes, wound so the pair share the apex-to-apex edge in opposite senses.
    // Precondition: `corner` is canonical.
    NeedleFacesOfEdge(self: PolygonMesh3D, corner: CornerIndex): Array<Array<VertexIndex>>
    {
        var near = self.ApexVertex(self.CornerFace(corner));
        var far = self.ApexVertex(self.CornerFace(self.TwinCorner(corner)));
        return [[self.CornerVertex(corner), far, near],
                [self.CornerDestination(corner), near, far]];
    }

    // One apex per face; two triangles per undirected edge.
    Needle(self: PolygonMesh3D, height: Number): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMeshOfFaces(
            Concatenate(self.Positions, self.FaceApexPoints(height)),
            self.EdgeStitchFaces((m, c) => m.NeedleFacesOfEdge(c)));
```
